issue.title: Deterministic scan: replace PyTorch's custom kernel with CCCL
issue.body:
## Background PyTorch's [deterministic cumulative sum](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/cuda/cub.cuh#L457) (used when `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` is set) runs a custom CUDA kernel in two passes: the first pass adds up each block, the second pass reads the input again and scans each block starting from the sum of the blocks before it. Doing it this way keeps the add order fixed, so the result is the same every run, but it reads the input twice. Scan speed is limited by memory, so that extra read means this approach can only reach about 66% (2 of 3 memory passes) of the speed a single-pass scan can hit. CCCL now makes `cub::DeviceScan` reproducible on its own through a `run_to_run` env knob ([CCCL PR #9098](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl/pull/9098)), will be available in the upcoming CCCL 3.5 release. (Check here for the related blogpost [Controlling Floating Point Determinism in NVIDIA CCCL](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/controlling-floating-point-determinism-in-nvidia-cccl/), and [docs] (https://nvidia.github.io/cccl/unstable/cccl/determinism.html)). Building against the latest CCCL, instead of the copy that ships with the CUDA toolkit, lets us delete the custom kernel and call `DeviceScan` instead. ## Build change: fetch CCCL from GitHub Today PyTorch uses CCCL from the headers bundled inside the CUDA toolkit (CTK). The `run_to_run` deterministic scan arrives in CCCL 3.5 (upcoming release), which is newer than the CCCL any released CTK ships with, so adopting it means building PyTorch against CCCL 3.5 instead of the toolkit's copy. There are a few ways to make this possible, one we tried locally is to do CMake fetch that pulls latest CCCL (master) from GitHub and prepends it to the include path, ahead of the toolkit's copy. This is safe because of CCCL's [compatibility policy](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl#cuda-toolkit-ctk-compatibility): the latest CCCL stays backward compatible with the current and previous CTK major versions (two major versions), and CCCL can be upgraded on its own, independently of the toolkit. So PyTorch keeps building against the CUDA version it already uses, with only the CCCL headers moved forward. ## Determinism usage The whole deterministic path becomes a single `DeviceScan` call with a `run_to_run` env: ```cpp auto env = ::cuda::std::execution::env{ stream, ::cuda::execution::require(::cuda::execution::determinism::run_to_run), caching_allocator_resource{}}; cub::DeviceScan::InclusiveSum(input, output, num_items, env); ``` ## Lines of code (`cub.cuh`, scan only) | | Lines | |---|---| | Removed (custom two-pass kernel + helpers) | - 126 | | Added (CCCL `DeviceScan` path) | + 21 | | **Net** | **-105** | ## Performance PyTorch's two-pass kernel at best reaches a peak of 32%, while the new CCCL's `cub::DeviceScan` reaches about 91% on large inputs, because it reads the input once instead of twice, also because of the latest warp specialized kernel (warpspeed-lookahead-scan).
NVIDIA B200 - cumsum, fp32 (Ref = current PyTorch, Cmp = CCCL) | Elements | Ref Time | Ref Noise | Cmp Time | Cmp Noise | Diff | %Diff | Status | |------------|------------|-------------|------------|-------------|--------------|---------|----------| | 2^16 | 20.942 us | 7.12% | 23.195 us | 12.79% | 2.253 us | 10.76% | 🔴 SLOW | | 2^18 | 21.356 us | 3.12% | 23.387 us | 53.42% | 2.031 us | 9.51% | 🔴 SLOW | | 2^20 | 22.739 us | 5.02% | 25.528 us | 5.56% | 2.789 us | 12.26% | 🔴 SLOW | | 2^22 | 33.401 us | 5.80% | 31.403 us | 5.37% | -1.998 us | -5.98% | 🟢 FAST | | 2^24 | 78.007 us | 1.27% | 48.413 us | 38.83% | -29.594 us | -37.94% | 🟢 FAST | | 2^26 | 249.637 us | 0.90% | 104.738 us | 2.13% | -144.898 us | -58.04% | 🟢 FAST | | 2^28 | 904.171 us | 0.71% | 336.952 us | 0.52% | -567.219 us | -62.73% | 🟢 FAST | | 2^30 | 3.508 ms | 0.24% | 1.254 ms | 0.50% | -2254.109 us | -64.26% | 🟢 FAST | | 2^32 | 13.888 ms | 0.10% | 4.922 ms | 0.08% | -8965.687 us | -64.56% | 🟢 FAST |
On large inputs CCCL is up to **2.8x faster** (2^32: 13.9 ms -> 4.9 ms), starting from about 1.6x at 2^24 and staying near 2.8x for the biggest sizes. ## Takeaway Building against the latest CCCL, instead of the version bundled with the CUDA toolkit (CTK), is what makes this work and it is seamless. We remove 105 lines of hand-written scan code and get a faster, reproducible `DeviceScan` in return. As CCCL adds more features, staying on the latest version lets PyTorch use them right away instead of waiting for a toolkit release. cc @ptrblck @msaroufim @eqy @tinglvv @nWEIdia @mruberry @kurtamohler

issue.title: Large cumulative sums appear to be nondeterministic.
issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

@timothytmzhou and I found that cumulative sums over large input arrays do not seem to deterministically produce the same output array:

```python
import torch
import math
import random
import numpy as np
import os

# make ourselves as deterministic as possible.
os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"] = ":4096:8"
np.random.seed(0)
torch.manual_seed(0)
random.seed(0)
torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False

# (deterministic) messy number generator
v = torch.Tensor([(x*math.pi)%1 for x in range(1000000)]).to(torch.device("cuda"))

# init a and b to the same cumulative sum.
a = b = v.cumsum(0)
counter = 0

# this loop should never terminate.
while ((a==b).all()):
	b = v.cumsum(0)
	counter+=1

print(f"non-determinism after {counter} runs.")
print("errors:",(a-b).abs()[a-b!=0])
print("first error index:",torch.where((a-b)!=0)[0][0])
```
yields, on my machine:
```
non-determinism after 1 runs.
errors: tensor([0.0020, 0.0020, 0.0020,  ..., 0.2188, 0.2188, 0.2188], device='cuda:0')
first error index: tensor(38400, device='cuda:0')
```
Multiple runs of this file exhibit unique non-determinism. Here's another run:
```
non-determinism after 1 runs.
errors: tensor([0.0039, 0.0039, 0.0039,  ..., 0.0938, 0.0938, 0.0938], device='cuda:0')
first error index: tensor(76800, device='cuda:0')
```
We decided to test this after reading [this paper](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/homes/lintan/publications/variance-ase20.pdf). Of note is the following paragraph:

> Scheduling and floating-point precision: GPU programming uses warp as a unit of computation. A warp consists of 32 parallel threads with concurrent memory access. Due to the limited precision (32-bits) of DL models, rounding errors are introduced at every step of floating-point calculation. In the GPU model, concurrent accesses to a single memory address must be serialized to prevent race conditions with no guaranteed order of access. Therefore, the rounding error introduced in each warp may vary across fixed-seed identical training runs due to the different accessing orders.

issue.title: [Bug]: vLLM produces wrong/corrupted embeddings for long inputs on Ascend NPU (chunked prefill related)
issue.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>The output of `python collect_env.py`</summary>

```text
Your output of above commands here
```

</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary / 概述

**EN:** When serving the embedding model `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` with `--runner pooling` via the **vLLM-Ascend** build (`quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.23.0-310p`, Ascend 310P), inputs longer than roughly 4000–8000 tokens intermittently produce **completely wrong embedding vectors**. The cosine similarity between this service and references (a reference service based on NVIDIA T4 + vLLM, the mis-tei service, and the official Modelscope online API of the same model) collapses from `>0.999` to `~0.2–0.6`. The corruption is deterministic per serve-session but changes across restarts, and is **entirely fixed by adding `--no-enable-chunked-prefill`**.

**CN:** 使用 **vLLM-Ascend** 构建（`quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.23.0-310p`，昇腾 310P）以 `--runner pooling` 部署 embedding 模型 `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` 时，约 4000–8000 tokens 以上的长输入会**间歇性地产生完全错误的 embedding 向量**。该服务与参考服务（基于英伟达 T4 + vLLM 的服务、mis-tei、以及同模型的 Modelscope 官方在线 API）之间的余弦相似度会从 `>0.999` 跌到 `~0.2–0.6`。该错误在同一个 serve 会话内是确定性的、但重启后会变化，并且**加 `--no-enable-chunked-prefill` 后完全消失**。

## Environment / 环境

- **EN:** vLLM version: **0.23.0** · Image: **`quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.23.0-310p`** · Python 3.11 · OS: Linux · Accelerator: **Ascend 310P** · Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` (Modelscope, `vllm serve ./Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`) · Served with `--runner pooling`, `--dtype float16`
- **CN:** vLLM 版本 **0.23.0** · 镜像：**`quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.23.0-310p`** · Python 3.11 · 操作系统 Linux · 加速卡：**昇腾 310P** · 模型 `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`（Modelscope，`vllm serve ./Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`）· `--runner pooling`、`--dtype float16`

## Reproduction / 复现步骤

### 1. Server startup / 服务端启动命令

```bash
vllm serve ./Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1024,512]}' \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": false}}' \
  --runner pooling --dtype float16 --port 8000
```

### 2. Client script / 客户端脚本（单条请求，batch size 1）

```python
import requests

URL = "http://localhost:8000/v1/embeddings"
TEXT = open("红楼梦.txt", encoding="utf-8").read()  # any long Chinese novel text
START, LEN = 26225, 10000  # e.g. 10k chars -> ~8k tokens

resp = requests.post(URL, json={
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B",
    "input": [TEXT[START:START + LEN]],
    # note: also reproduced WITHOUT the following two params
    "truncate_prompt_tokens": -1,
    "truncation_side": "right",
}).json()
vec = resp["data"][0]["embedding"]   # 1024-dim
```

### 3. Reference / 正确参考

Same input encoded with the following services as "correct" reference / 同一输入用以下服务编码作为"正确"参考：

- **T4 + vLLM reference service**: the same model served on **NVIDIA T4 + vLLM** / 基于**英伟达 T4 + vLLM** 部署的同模型服务
- **mis-tei service** (`qwen3-embeddings-doc-base`, same model weight) / 同为该模型权重的 mis-tei 服务
- Official Modelscope online API for `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` / Modelscope 官方在线 API：
  `curl https://api-inference.modelscope.cn/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B","input":["<text>"],"encoding_format":"float"}'`

Similarity is cosine similarity on the raw 1024-dim vectors / 相似度为 1024 维原始向量间的余弦相似度。

## Expected vs. Actual / 期望与实际

- **EN (Expected)**: cosine(vllm, mis-tei/online) ≥ 0.999 for all input lengths. / **Actual**: for long / table-like inputs, cosine drops to ~0.2–0.6, and vLLM output is **not self-consistent** (tiny input changes flip the whole vector).
- **CN (期望)**: 任意输入长度下 cosine(vllm, mis-tei/online) ≥ 0.999。/ **实际**: 长文本/表格类输入时余弦跌到 ~0.2–0.6，且 vLLM 输出**自身不一致**（输入只改一点点，整个向量就翻转）。

## Evidence / 证据

### A. Small prefix change flips the entire embedding (deterministic) / 前缀微变导致整个向量翻转（确定性）

Same start offset. First row: cross-service comparison below the threshold (the two services agree); rest: within Ascend vLLM, lengths differ by only a few chars / 相同起点；第一行为跨服务对比（未超阈值时两服务一致），其余为 Ascend vLLM 内部仅相差几个字符长度的自比：

| comparison / 对比 | cosine |
|---|---|
| Ascend vLLM (len 4200) vs mis-tei (len 4200) | 0.998 |
| Ascend vLLM (len 4480) vs Ascend vLLM (len 4500) | **0.35** |
| Ascend vLLM (len 4496) vs Ascend vLLM (len 4500) | **0.36** |
| Ascend vLLM (len 4498) vs Ascend vLLM (len 4500) | **0.93** |

Adding just 20 chars (or even 2 chars) flips the vector from ~0.93 to ~0.35 similarity. Same input is deterministic across calls — a real numerical issue, not noise / 仅增加 20 字符（甚至 2 字符）相似度就从 0.93 翻到 0.35；同一输入多次调用结果一致，属真实数值问题而非随机噪声。

mis-tei does NOT show this: `mis-tei(4200) vs mis-tei(4700)` = 0.997 (smooth) / mis-tei 无此现象：`mis-tei(4200) vs mis-tei(4700)` = 0.997（平滑）。

### B. Cross-service: Ascend vLLM vs T4 reference vs Modelscope online / 跨服务对比

During a broken serve session, 10 random 38k-char slices / 异常会话期间，10 条随机 3.8 万字符切片：

| metric / 指标 | value / 值 |
|---|---|
| Ascend vLLM (buggy) vs T4 + vLLM reference | 0.22 – 0.61 (avg ≈ 0.37) |
| T4 + vLLM reference vs mis-tei | 0.98 |
| T4 + vLLM reference vs Modelscope online | ≥ 0.99999 |

The reference services agree with each other (T4 + vLLM reference and online = Modelscope API, cosine ≥ 0.99999); mis-tei also agrees with them to ~0.98. So the reference is trustworthy and the wrong vectors are specific to the **vLLM-Ascend build on 310P**, not to vLLM in general (the same model + config on NVIDIA T4 + vLLM is correct) / 参考服务互相一致（T4 + vLLM 参考服务与在线 = Modelscope API，余弦 ≥ 0.99999）；mis-tei 与其也一致到 ~0.98。故参考可信，错误向量**特指昇腾 310P 上的 vLLM-Ascend 构建**，而非 vLLM 通用问题（同一模型+配置在英伟达 T4 + vLLM 上是正确的）。

### C. Length threshold / 长度阈值（同 10 个起点，平均）

| length chars / 字符数 | ≈ tokens / 约多少 tokens | Ascend vLLM (buggy) vs T4 + vLLM reference, avg / 平均 | abnormal? / 是否异常 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2000 | 1700 | 0.999995 | no / 否 |
| 5000 | 4200 | 0.96–1.0 | borderline / 临界 |
| 10000 | 8000 | **0.17 – 0.5** | **yes / 是** |
| 15000+ | 12000+ | 0.17 – 0.5 (no further degradation) / （不再继续劣化） | **yes / 是** |

Once over the threshold the whole vector is wrong; it is not gradual drift / 一旦超过阈值整个向量就错了，并非渐进漂移。

### D. After restart with `--no-enable-chunked-prefill` / 加该参数重启后

Same 10 start offsets, 2000→40000 chars (up to ~32768 tokens = context limit) / 同 10 个起点，2000→40000 字符（最高约 32768 tokens = 上下文上限）：

| length chars / 字符数 | vLLM vs T4 reference | vLLM vs Modelscope online |
|---|---|---|
| 2000–6000 | 0.999996 | 0.999996 |
| 10000–12000 | 0.999996 | 0.999996 (≤9000 only) / 仅 ≤9000 |
| 14000–40000 | 0.99999+ | (skipped, online ≤8192 tokens) / 跳过 |

**Bug completely disappears.** vLLM now matches the T4 reference / online at 0.99999+ across the full range / **问题完全消失**，vLLM 在整个范围内与 T4 参考 / 在线保持 0.99999+ 一致。

## What was tested / ruled out / 已测试 / 已排除项

- `truncate_prompt_tokens: -1` + `truncation_side: right` → **no effect / 无影响**（有无这两个参数都能复现）
- `--no-enable-prefix-caching` → **no effect / 无影响**
- `--no-enable-chunked-prefill` → **fixes the bug / 修复问题**
- The corruption is **intermittent across restarts**; within a broken session it is deterministic / 错误**重启后间歇出现**；异常会话内确定。
- Same model + config on **NVIDIA T4 + vLLM (T4 reference)** is **correct** at all lengths → issue is specific to vLLM-Ascend (310P), not vLLM generally / 同模型同配置在**英伟达 T4 + vLLM（T4 参考）上全程正确** → 问题特指 vLLM-Ascend（310P），非 vLLM 通用问题。
- Batch size 1, single request only. A concurrent locust load test existed on the same cluster in some sessions — broken sessions behaved like *affected by earlier concurrent load*, which also suggested chunked prefill / 单条请求（bs=1）；部分异常会话期间集群上有并发压测在跑，异常表现疑似受先前并发负载影响，这也是怀疑 chunked prefill 的原因。

## Suggested root cause / 可能的根因

While chunked prefill is enabled, the encoder (`--runner pooling`) in the **vLLM-Ascend build on 310P** likely computes the pooler on a **chunked / partial hidden-state view** for long inputs (≥ one chunk boundary), producing a valid but numerically wrong vector. The T4-based vLLM reference handles the same input correctly, so this looks Ascend-specific in the encoder path. Disabling chunked prefill forces single-pass prefill so the pooler sees all hidden states / 开启 chunked prefill 时，**310P 上的 vLLM-Ascend** 编码器（`--runner pooling`）对长输入可能只用**分块的、部分 hidden-state** 来计算 pooler（长度跨过一个 chunk 边界时触发），产出数值上明显错误的向量。T4 上的 vLLM 参考服务处理同一输入是正常的，说明这疑似昇腾编码器路径特有。关闭 chunked prefill 后强制单次 prefill，pooler 能看到完整 hidden states。

## Workaround / 规避方法

Start the server with `--no-enable-chunked-prefill` / 加如下参数启动服务：

```bash
vllm serve ./Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
  --runner pooling --dtype float16 \
  --no-enable-chunked-prefill --port 8000
```

(Workaround verified: full 2000→40000-char sweep matches reference services at 0.99999+ / 已验证：2000→40000 字符全量扫描与参考服务一致，0.99999+。)
